bank_name: South Bangla Agriculture & Commerce Bank PLC
period_note: MIXED-BASIS FILING, DIFFERENT STRUCTURE FROM FY2023-2025: unlike this bank's FY2023-2025 quarterly filings (which each print a full separate plain/Solo Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss Account after the Consolidated ones), this 84-page filing prints ONLY a full Consolidated Balance Sheet and Consolidated Profit and Loss Account as its primary statements -- Solo (Bank-only, i.e. excluding subsidiary SBAC Bank Investment Limited) figures are recoverable only as sub-rows within individual notes (e.g. Note 36 taxation, Note 37.1 NAV, Note 38.1 EPS) or via two further single-purpose annexures (Annexure B: Islamic Banking Windows; a further annexure: Off-shore Banking Unit), not as one reconstructable full Solo balance sheet. Given this, total_assets/total_liabilities/total_equity/total_deposits/gross_loans/off_balance_sheet_exposures/paid_up_capital/reserves and all P&L cumulative lines below are CONSOLIDATED (the only basis for which a complete, internally-consistent statement is printed); the resulting ROA/ROE/LDR are therefore also Consolidated-basis. Where the Bank's own notes DO give a clean Solo (of-the-Bank) figure, it is recorded as supplementary context in this note rather than substituted into the primary fields (to avoid a mixed-basis balance-sheet identity within this record): NAV per share of the Bank (Note 37.1) is 13.95 vs 14.00 Consolidated; EPS of the Bank (Note 38.1) is 0.14 (PAT Tk.115,637,550) vs 0.14 Consolidated (PAT Tk.115,719,077, rounds the same); shareholders' equity of the Bank (Note 37.1) is Tk.11,498,951,736 vs Tk.11,539,099,056 Consolidated -- the subsidiary's contribution remains small (0.35% of equity) but is no longer as negligible as in FY2021-2022 (then <0.01%). BY CONTRAST, classified_loans/npl_pct/provision_required/provision_maintained/provision_surplus_deficit below ARE Solo-basis (Note 8.10/8.11, On-shore + Off-shore Banking Unit only, excluding the investment subsidiary) -- this matches the established convention already documented in this dataset's sources.json for FY2023-2025 (where Note 8.10/8.11 is confirmed Solo-basis by document position and an 'on solo basis' capital sentence nearby). Because classified_loans is Solo-basis, npl_pct here is deliberately computed against the matching SOLO total-loans denominator from the same Note 8.10/8.11 (Tk.94,675,639,202), NOT the Consolidated gross_loans figure used elsewhere in this record (Tk.94,911,900,233, which includes the subsidiary) -- using a mismatched denominator would understate the ratio; this basis choice is documented per-item below. CONTINUING CRISIS, STILL SEVERE BUT IMPROVING FROM FY2025 YEAR-END: Solo NPL fell to 18.50% (Tk.17,516,895,254 classified) from 19.92% at 31-Dec-2025 (Tk.18,814,937,629) -- still far above the 5-6% range seen through FY2023. The loans-and-advances provision shortfall (Note 8.10) also narrowed to Tk.7,461,629,290 (required 10,983,143,743 vs maintained 3,521,514,453) from Tk.10,235,750,153 at 31-Dec-2025 (matching this bank's own 2025_Q4.json/insights.json qualified-opinion figure exactly). Note 8.10's own footnote cites Bangladesh Bank letter ref. BSD-5/106/2026-389 (26 April 2026, quantifying the auditors' own required-vs-maintained figures) and a SEPARATE letter ref. BSD-5/106/2026-403 (28 April 2026) permitting finalization of these Q1-2026 financial statements without adjusting for the remaining shortfall -- the LATTER is the SAME letter number already documented in this bank's insights.json as the one directing no FY2025 dividend, confirming it also covers this interim filing. No capital-adequacy (CRAR/RWA/Tier1/Tier2) disclosure found anywhere in this 84-page filing, consistent with every prior quarter in this bank's archive.
